name: East Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Steep heather and talus leads to an obvious notch (~5,600 ft) on the ESE ridge.
From the notch, trend left across class 3 rock to a short, exposed 20-ft class 4 step just below the true summit; most parties rope up for this section.

rappel_detail.notes: The one rappel most parties make: a 60 m rope doubled clears the step. Two more short slung stations sit at steeper steps lower on the ridge; parties use them on loose or wet rock, or downclimb those steps at Class 3-4.
rappel_detail.anchor: tree or rock horn with webbing and rap rings (climber-maintained, not bolted)
hazards: Climber-maintained tat: inspect it and back it up or replace it.
Loose, dirty rock around the second step; keep the party close, the ridge is exposed on both sides.
rappel_detail.station: The first fixed anchor, at the steepest, most exposed step just below the summit block on the East Ridge (the short Class 4 crux).

rappels: One rappel (or a handline) over the short Class 4 step below the summit block; up to two more optional short rappels from slung stations lower on the ridge
descent_text: Descent reverses the East Ridge line back to the 5,600 ft notch and down into the basin, then back up and over Bumblebee Pass to rejoin the PCT for the hike out. On the ridge itself, established rappel stations exist at up to three short steps, marked by fixed/fresh webbing and rappel rings threaded on rock horns (not bolted). The crux is a short ~20 ft Class 4 step just below the summit block — most parties either rappel it, rig a handline, or downclimb it if comfortable. One or two additional short rappel/downclimb sections lie higher on the ridge and are optional; confident scramblers downclimb Class 3 terrain there instead of building an anchor. A 30-35m single rope (or a doubled rope) reaches the anchors for all three stations, though at least one pitch has been reported to run close to the limit of a 30m rope, so carrying a 35-40m single rope (or rapping on doubled strands from a 60m) gives more margin. Watch for loose, dirty rock, particularly around the second rappel/downclimb section, and keep parties tight since the ridge is exposed on both sides. Once back at the basin, reclimb roughly 300 ft over Bumblebee Pass before descending to Ridge Lake and the PCT for the return hike to the trailhead.
approach: From the PCT North Trailhead at I-90 Exit 52 (~3,000 ft), follow the Pacific Crest Trail north through Commonwealth Basin and up onto the Kendall Ridge switchbacks. At roughly 5.5-5.7 miles you reach the Kendall Katwalk, the exposed rock traverse blasted into the cliff band that most parties use as a progress checkpoint. Continue north past Ridge Lake and Gravel/Alaska Lake — the last reliable water before the high basin and ridge — for another 0.3-2 miles to the base of Bumblebee Pass. A short, steep, unmaintained climbers' path (loose tread, care warranted with a pack) climbs to the 5,400 ft pass, then drops down the north side into the open basin directly below Mount Thomson's south face (this basin doubles as the standard camp for West Ridge parties). From the basin, aim for the steep heather-and-talus slope leading to an obvious notch at about 5,600 ft on the East (ESE) Ridge — loose talus and minor route-finding here are the main approach-specific hazards. From the notch, scramble up and traverse left (mostly Class 2-3) along the ridge crest to the base of the final summit block. Total one-way distance from the trailhead to the summit is roughly 8 miles, and the round trip gains about 4,900 ft (the up-and-over at Bumblebee Pass adds extra elevation beyond the net summit height). Expect a long day: parties commonly report 3-5 hours car-to-basin and a full 9-11 hour round trip.
overview: The East Ridge is Mount Thomson's easiest natural line and the standard descent for parties climbing the West Ridge. It's sustained Class 3 scrambling on solid rock with one short, exposed Class 4 chimney (~20 ft) just below the summit. The peak's original 1917 ascent (Joe Hazard and B. French) is generally attributed to an easy east-side line like this one, though no published account gives the exact route taken.
beta: Considered the easiest way up Mount Thomson and the standard descent for the West Ridge as well. After the long PCT approach to Bumblebee Pass and down into the basin, a steep heather-and-talus slope gains an obvious notch (~5,600 ft) on the peak's ESE ridge; from there the route trends left across class 3 terrain to a short, exposed 20-ft class 4 step guarding the true summit, which most parties protect with a rope.
gear: Small rack or slings for backing up rappel anchors
